test_command: dotnet build api/Biolog.Api/Biolog.Api.csproj && dotnet test tests/dotnet/Biolog.IntegrationTests/Biolog.IntegrationTests.csproj && dotnet test tests/dotnet/Biolog.UnitTests/Biolog.UnitTests.csproj && dotnet test tests/features/bio-dev-004/Biolog.Features.DeviceOperations.Tests.csproj && bash scripts/check-module-project-references.sh && python3 scripts/check-traceability.py --all && bash scripts/secret-scan.sh && (cd web && npx tsc --noEmit) && (cd tests/frontend && npx vitest run) && (cd tests/frontend && npx playwright test bio-dev-004-device-operations)
notes:
BIO-DEV-004 round 2 - fixes SY-DEV004-01 (Seyi, round 1, Critical): all four BIO-DEV-004 routes (GET /, POST /{id}/poll-health, GET /{id}/remote-job-capabilities, POST /{id}/remote-jobs) previously had zero provenance/RBAC gating, and the two mutating routes derived the audit actor directly from caller-controlled request JSON (ActorType/ActorId fields), letting any caller run a real remote reboot/configuration/firmware job and attribute it to an arbitrary actor.

Fix: ported the canonical ActorProvenanceGate + IPermissionGateway pattern (ADR-0006 Decision 3), same shape as BIO-TRN-003/BIO-INT-004/BIO-ATT-003, verbatim where possible (Api/ActorProvenanceGate.cs, Api/ActorResolver.cs copied from BIO-TRN-003's own identical gate - this project cannot reference that sibling feature project either). New internal Domain/IPermissionGateway.cs + PermissionRequiredException, wired in BioDev004Module.cs via a PermissionGatewayAdapter wrapping BIO-IDN-006's own already-registered PermissionService.ActorHasPermissionAsync (DependsOn now includes "Rbac").

Two distinct, least-privilege permission keys per Seyi's explicit requirement ("require separate least-privilege tenant permissions for device read/health polling and remote-job execution"): DeviceHealthPollingService.ReadPermission ("device_operations.read" - list devices, poll health, read remote-job capabilities) and DeviceRemoteJobService.ExecutePermission ("device_operations.execute" - actually running a job). Capabilities-read uses the lower-privilege read permission since it's informational; running a job needs the strictly higher execute permission - an actor who can see what a device supports cannot necessarily run anything against it (proven by a dedicated test).

The audit actor is now derived ONLY from the verified X-Actor-Id/X-Actor-Provenance headers via ActorResolver - DeviceHeartbeatRequest/RemoteJobRequest no longer carry ActorType/ActorId fields at all, closing the forgeable-audit-actor half of the finding (the exact contract Seyi's own integration-test proof pointed at).

Added web/lib/actor-provenance-routes.ts's own DeviceOperations entry (two precise regex matches scoped to exactly this story's own four routes, never the bare /api/v1/devices prefix - BIO-DEV-001's own POST //GET /{id} and BIO-DEV-003's own GET /{id}/capabilities //{id}/health deliberately remain unmatched, since they stay ungated per those stories' own disclosed scope, not this story's to expand into). web/features/bio-dev-004/live.ts switched from a request-body ActorType/ActorId pair to a static ACTOR_HEADERS (X-Actor-Id/X-Actor-Type) - the same disclosed boundary BIO-TRN-003's/BIO-INT-004's own live adapters already established (SIMULATION-mode Playwright proves the mapped workflow; the real HTTP endpoints - RBAC/provenance included - are proven directly against the real backend).

Tests: 3 new feature-unit tests (permission-denied on read, permission-denied on execute-but-not-read, read-without-execute can see capabilities but cannot run a job) - 16/16 feature-unit total. 5 new real-host integration tests in BioDev004EndpointsTests.cs (missing X-Actor-Id -> 400; missing X-Actor-Provenance -> 401; a provenance proof computed for a DIFFERENT actor id than the one asserted -> 401, the exact forged-attribution shape named; an actor with no ReadPermission -> 403 on list AND poll, not a silently-filtered 200; an actor with ReadPermission but not ExecutePermission can read capabilities but is refused running a job, with no audit event recorded) - every pre-existing functional test now runs through an authorized caller with a real resolved actor + valid provenance proof against a test-controllable permission gateway (MutableFakePermissionGateway, same shape BIO-ATT-003's own WorkforceAttendanceEndpointsIntegrationTests uses - chosen over seeding real BIO-IDN-006 RBAC grants because this class's own per-test unique tenant ids, needed to prove certification/cross-tenant isolation, would otherwise require a real grant seeded per tenant, re-proving BIO-IDN-006's own PermissionService rather than this story's own gating/wiring). 279/279 integration total (265 original + 9 round-1 + 5 new), 210/210 unit (no regression), module-reference/secret-scan/traceability all PASS, tsc clean, vitest 550/550 (unaffected - mock ports never called the real HTTP endpoints), Playwright 6/6 re-run 3x stable (SIMULATION mode, unaffected by the backend authorization change for the same reason).

Also added a BioDev004Module.Configure() synthetic-tenant grant seed (mirrors BioTrn003Module's own - seeds both new permission keys for RoleType.TenantAdmin onto WebSessionBridge:SyntheticTenantId when configured, fail-closed/inert otherwise) so a real demo-bridge browser session can reach an authorized state too, matching god's instruction to 'wire the live browser path through the signed-session provenance bridge.'
